claims.claim: The strongest evidence is the SELECT trial, a large randomized, placebo-controlled study of 17,604 adults with overweight or obesity, established cardiovascular disease, and no diabetes.
The average follow-up was about 3 years.
claims.note: atomic part of a compound sentence

claims.claim: Weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the relative risk of cardiovascular death, nonfatal heart attack, or nonfatal stroke by 20% compared with placebo.
claims.note: atomic part of a compound sentence

claims.claim: The events occurred in 6.5% of participants taking semaglutide versus 8.0% taking placebo—an absolute difference of 1.5 percentage points.

citations.note: the page is real but does not say this

citations.quote: The primary outcome, major adverse CV events (MACE: composite of CV death, nonfatal MI, and nonfatal stroke), for semaglutide vs. placebo, was: 6.5% vs. 8.0% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.72-0.90, p < 0.001).

claims.claim: Separate trials have also found cardiovascular benefit from GLP-1 drugs in people with type 2 diabetes.
The size of benefit and the groups studied vary by medication and trial.
claims.note: atomic part of a compound sentence

claims.claim: SELECT’s result should not be assumed to apply equally to everyone or to every GLP-1 drug.
claims.note: atomic part of a compound sentence

claims.claim: In SELECT, gastrointestinal side effects led more people to stop semaglutide.

citations.quote: Semaglutide was stopped more frequently than placebo for gastrointestinal intolerance, a known side effect of this class of medications; however, there was no higher rate of serious gastrointestinal events. The researchers noted that this medication did not lead to an increased rate of pancreatitis, which has been a concern with prior medications of this type.
